newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ABDUR-RAHIM UNANIMOUS CHOICE FOR 1996-97 ALL-ROOKIE TEAM.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ABDUR-RAHIM UNANIMOUS CHOICE FOR 1996-97 ALL-ROOKIE TEAM.

text.p: Vancouver Grizzlies forward Shareef Abdur-Rahim was the lone unanimous choice in voting for the 1996-97 NBA All-Rookie Team announced by the league on Tuesday.

Abdur-Rahim was joined by NBA Rookie of the Year Allen Iverson of the Philadelphia 76ers, guard Stephon Marbury of the Minnesota Timberwolves and forwards Marcus Camby of the Toronto Raptors and Antoine Walker of the Boston Celtics.

The All-Rookie Team was determined by voting from the league's 29 head coaches. With coaches not allowed to vote for players on their own team, Abdur-Rahim was the only player named to the first team on the maximum 28 ballots.
The Vancouver forward received 56 points in the voting, based on two points for a first team selection and one for a second team choice.
Sixers guard Iverson, who last week won the league's top rookie award, and Marbury each received 55 points, while Camby and Walker garnered 48 points.
Iverson and Marbury also were named on 28 ballots.

Getting the All-Rookie second team nod were four guards -- New Jersey's Kerry Kittles, Milwaukee's Ray Allen, the Los Angeles Lakers' Kobe Bryant and Houston's Matt Maloney -- and Lakers centre Travis Knight.
